roles.heroLead: An island house is never quite dry — salt air outside, shower steam inside, winter damp in between. Tile and grout won't hold that water back; the membrane behind them does. So we build the hidden assembly first, run a 24-hour flood test, photograph it, and only then open a box of tile.
roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost on Whidbey Island, WA?
roles.costP1: Across Whidbey Island, tile installation prices at $14–$26 per square foot installed — that's tile, labor, substrate prep and setting materials combined, with labor alone from $11/sq ft. A tub-shower surround typically lands at $3,200–$6,800; a whole bathroom of floor, shower and niche runs $6,500–$14,000, and a bathroom floor by itself (about 45 sq ft) goes for $900–$1,600.
roles.costP2: One thing the ferry teaches is that the sticker never tells the whole story. Same with tile: a $4 mosaic sheet often costs more on the wall than $12 large-format porcelain, because installation labor tracks cuts and grout lines rather than what the box cost.
roles.costNote: Installed ranges for island homes as of August 2026 — tile plus materials plus labor. The written quote from your free visit is the one that binds.
roles.layersLead: Seven layers, and every one earns its ferry ticket. When a shower fails and we open it up, a layer was skipped — the membrane, almost always: a few hundred dollars saved once, a five-figure rebuild later.
roles.whyP1: Island moisture is patient, and a shower leak is more patient still. Water works through grout, settles into the substrate, and shows itself a couple of winters later — a soft floor outside the bathroom door, a mark on the ceiling underneath. By then the job is framing, subfloor and drywall first, new tile second.
roles.whyP2: Waterproofing is roughly a tenth of a shower's price. On a damp island, leaving it out is the costliest shortcut going.

roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost on Whidbey Island, WA?
roles.faqA1: On Whidbey Island, tile installation runs $14 to $26 per square foot installed when you count tile, labor, setting materials and substrate prep — labor starts at $11 per square foot by itself. A standard tub-shower surround comes to $3,200–$6,800, a roughly 45 sq ft bathroom floor to $900–$1,600, and a complete bath — floor, shower and niche — to $6,500–$14,000. Format is the real price lever: mosaic sheets and large-format tile both take considerably more labor than a simple 12×12.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower on Whidbey Island?
roles.faqA2: A standard alcove shower on Whidbey Island prices between $3,200 and $6,800 — demo of the old surround, a pre-sloped pan, the bonded waterproofing system, tile setting, niche and grout all included. Curbless entries, benches, steam units and full-height stone climb from there. Waterproofing accounts for about a tenth of the price, and in an island climate it's the tenth doing all the heavy lifting.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Without exception — on an island, doubly so. Each shower gets a pre-sloped base, a bonded ANSI A118.10 membrane run up the walls following TCNA methods, sealed seams, corners and pipe penetrations, then a documented 24-hour flood test with photos before tile goes anywhere near the walls. Tile and grout merely shed water; the membrane is the actual barrier keeping it out of your framing.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: Four to six working days for most Whidbey Island bathrooms, with the ferry built into the schedule: demolition and dust protection first, then substrate and waterproofing with the 24-hour flood test running overnight, a day or two of tile setting, and a finish day of grout, silicone and trim. Grout needs a further 24 hours to cure before the shower sees water. A standalone floor is generally one to two days.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: In a marine climate, porcelain wins almost every argument: denser than ceramic, harder to chip, and absorbing less than 0.5% water — which matters when the whole house lives damp half the year. Ceramic still makes sense on walls and backsplashes, where it's cheaper and stays dry. Our island rule: porcelain underfoot and in every shower floor, ceramic or glass up on the walls.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes, and island winters make the case better than we can. An electric radiant mat adds $11–$16 per square foot installed with the thermostat, set over an uncoupling membrane, resistance-tested both before and after tiling, and powered from a dedicated circuit. It only pencils out while the floor is already open — retrofitting later means paying for the same floor twice.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Usually, yes. Tear-out including haul-away starts at $3.50/sq ft — and everything we pull leaves the island with us. More importantly, demo is the only real look at the subfloor: corroded fasteners, damp-swollen panels, movement, rot. Tiling over old tile can be done on a genuinely flat, sound floor, but it raises heights at doorways and buries the problems worth knowing about.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost on Whidbey Island?
roles.faqA8: Plan on $1,100–$2,200 installed for the usual 30 sq ft backsplash on Whidbey Island, with outlet cuts, edge trim and counter-matched grout in the price. The top of the range belongs to fussier layouts — herringbone, mosaic sheets, a picture-frame accent over the range, or slab-look porcelain carried to the ceiling.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Often, and for a beach cabin it's frequently the sensible spend. From $8 per square foot we handle stained or crumbling grout, tiles cracked by an impact, and shower corners due for silicone in place of grout. The exceptions: tile sounding hollow, loosening in a spreading pattern, or a wall soft to the touch — that's substrate failure, and a repair only rents you time. We'll say which one yours is before we write a number.
roles.faqQ10: Which Whidbey Island communities do you tile?
roles.faqA10: The whole island — Clinton, Langley, Freeland, Greenbank, Coupeville and Oak Harbor, along with the water-side communities between them: Bayview, Maxwelton, Scatchet Head, Sandy Hook, Possession Shores, Mutiny Bay, Bush Point, Lagoon Point, Admirals Cove and Penn Cove. On the mainland side we also serve Mukilteo, Everett and the wider Puget Sound.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: Tile installation from OC Flooring carries a 2-year workmanship warranty — longer than our carpet coverage on purpose, because a tile problem tends to appear in year two rather than week two. Where we install a manufacturer's complete waterproofing assembly, their system warranty applies alongside ours. And because the membrane and flood test are photographed on every job, the record survives — useful the day your island place goes on the market.
